News.title: Arsenal one result from Premier League title and have VAR to thank again
News.content:
Certainly it would have been even more fretful than it was if Havertz was dismissed. And it was very fretful.

If City do win – and Arsenal were the last side to take the points at Bournemouth – then it goes to the final day. Arsenal will be away to Crystal Palace and City are at home to Aston Villa.

To add extra drama we now know that will be Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge after 10 remarkable years at City. Will there be another twist?

If Arsenal win on Sunday, again they are champions. Otherwise they will simply have to match City’s result. No matter what happens before then their destiny is in their hands and that is a position they craved.

The disappointment for Arsenal here was they did not score more against Burnley as this was an opportunity to rack up a lead in terms of goal difference – which might also come into the equation – that they did not take.

But it was the win and, really, nothing but the win that mattered in what was absolutely a game of two contrasting halves. In the first, Arsenal were fully in control and should have scored more – Leandro Trossard hit a post, other chances were not taken, with Eberechi Eze later clipping the crossbar after the break. In the second it was almost backs-against-the-wall. Especially in that final 20 minutes when they yet again leant heavily on Declan Rice.

At the end the jubilant reaction was understandable. There were even tears of relief from some fans. After the stadium announcer called it – “1-0 to the Arsenal” – first captain Martin Odegaard and then Arteta took the mic as the players and staff stood around the centre circle in what looked like a choreographed approach before embarking on a lap of appreciation.

Sports.title: Antonio Conte ‘to leave Napoli amid Italy national team links’ with another ex-Chelsea boss set to replace him
Sports.content:
ANTONIO CONTE is reportedly set to leave Napoli at the end of the season amid growing links with the Italy national team job.

According to journalist Guillaume Pacini, Conte has decided to walk away from the Serie A champions despite still having one year remaining on his contract.





The report claims the former Chelsea boss is prepared to forgo both his final year of salary and any severance package worth around £15million in order to leave on good terms.

Conte famously guided Chelsea to the Premier League title in 2017, the last time the Blues were crowned champions of England.

The Italian has rebuilt his reputation in Serie A after leading Napoli to the league title, adding another major honour to his glittering managerial CV.

Speculation surrounding Conte’s future intensified almost immediately after Italy failed to qualify for the World Cup, with many fans and pundits tipping him as the ideal man to revive the national side.



While there is no suggestion he is heading to another club, the report states the Italy job is hugely appealing to him, although he could also decide to take a short break from management.

Journalist Guillaume Pacini wrote: Antonio Conte and Napoli, it’s over.

“The coach has decided to leave at the end of this season, he will forgo his final year of salary and any severance pay.”

He is the second high profile manager likely to walk away from his job this summer after Pep Guardiola.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Napoli are already said to be lining up a replacement.

And it could see another familiar face to Chelsea fans arrive in Naples.

Former Blues boss Maurizio Sarri has reportedly emerged as Napoli’s top target to replace Conte.

Sarri previously coached both Chelsea and Napoli, winning the Europa League during his spell at Stamford Bridge after making his name with the Italian outfit in Serie A.



The experienced coach has long been admired by Napoli supporters for the attacking style of football his side produced during his first spell in charge.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy ‘lined up for emotional transfer to former club’ as former England star, 39, close to becoming free agent
Sports.content:
SHEFFIELD WEDNESDAY are interested in signing Jamie Vardy this summer, according to reports.

Vardy, 39, has spent this season at Cremonese in Serie A.





The Sheffield-born striker is a boyhood Wednesday fan and was part of their academy between 1996 and 2002.

According to Wednesday reporter Joe Crann, Owls chiefs have discussed a potential swoop for Vardy.

Crann adds, however, that he reckons a return to Leicester would be more likely, should Vardy decide to drop down to League One.

The former England forward left the King Power last summer following 13 years with the club.

Vardy scored 200 goals in 500 appearances for the Foxes, winning the Premier League, FA Cup and two Championship titles during his stint.

Following his Leicester exit he penned a one-year deal with Serie A new boys Cremonese.

Vardy has managed seven goals in 28 Italian top flights outings, including two in his last two games.

Having previously looked doomed, back-to-back victories have seen Cremonese climb to within one point of safety ahead of the final day.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Vardy and Co are set to host Udinese this Sunday, while their relegation rivals Lecce welcome Genoa.

Wednesday, meanwhile, are set to play in League One following a two-year spell in the Championship.

The Owls finished on zero points in the second tier, having been docked 18 due to financial issues.

Earlier this month the crisis club were finally taken over, with confirmation that they will NOT face a points deduction in League One next season.

Sports.title: Move over Fergie and Ancelotti, managerial Superman Pep Guardiola is football’s undisputed Muhammad Ali
Sports.content:
IT IS not just the trophy count that means Pep Guardiola IS the greatest manager of all time – even if those are impressive enough numbers.

Six Premier League crowns, with a magnificent seventh still possible, if unlikely.



Three FA Cup and five League Cups. Plus the Champions League, Club World Cup and Uefa Super Cup, all with City.

Add in three LaLiga titles, two Champions League, Fifa and Uefa honours plus a couple of Cope del Reys at Barcelona, three Bundesliga triumphs and four other pieces of silverware at Bayern.

A staggering 35 major pots in all spread over 18 years, an average – given his 12-month sabbatical in New York before arriving in Bavaria – of more than two per season.



Yet it is more the legacy he leaves. Not just an inspirational manager, a winning manager, a manager every player wanted to play for.

But the most consequential one of the lot – because unlike the majority of the managerial legends, Guardiola has genuinely changed football.

This season might have seen the return of the percentage game, a prevalence of set-pieces and WWE being the route to success.

Yet that was, in itself, seen as an antidote to the changes wrought to English football by Guardiola and the “school” he has effectively introduced.

For years, seemingly forever, the game in this country was derided overseas as a barbarian concept. All about physicality and grit, muscle and strength.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Virtues which had a place but were no match, time and time again, for tactics and skill, game management and intelligence.

No longer. Just watch the Premier League, how almost every team wants to play, to maintain possession, to bait the press, seeking to pull opponents out of their shape and structure by pure football, not bang it and hope.

That you see it replicated in Leagues One and Two, non-league football, even on park pitches and by kids.

And that is Guardiola’s influence, more than anybody else.



He has a vision and will not be deflected.

It is sometimes hard to remember how in his first season at City, when they finished empty handed, his decision to dump England No 1 Joe Hart and bring in the gaffe-prone Claudio Bravo, saw Guardiola accused of biting off more than he could chew.

Now, of course, we can see it was not the plan but the man-power. Once he had Ederson, rather than the Chilean in goal, it all came together.

And while that City team had brilliance from across the world, Kevin de Bruyne and Vincent Kompany, Bernardo Silva and Sergio Aguero, to name just a few, look at the impact he had on Kyle Walker, John Stones, Phil Foden, Raheem Sterling and Nico O’Reilly.



There are rivals for the title, for sure.

In England, greats of the past like Matt Busby, Don Revie, Bill Shankly and Bill Nicholson. In the more modern era, Alex Ferguson, Arsene Wenger, Jose Mourinho and Jurgen Klopp.

Plus, never to be ignored, Helenio Herrera, Fabio Capello, Arrigo Sachi, Ernst Happel, Franz Beckenbauer, Marcello Lippi, Carlo Ancelotti, Miguel Munoz and Vicente del Bosque.

Few of them, if any, have had the same fundamental impact that Guardiola has on football.

And, of course, he has taken on and beaten many of them, too, whether on domestic fields or continental ones.



Fergie had no answer to Guardiola’s Barca, played off the pitch in Rome in 2009 and at Wembley two years later.

Wenger’s Arsenal were in decline, Klopp could win the Prem crown just once against him, while Mourinho was driven almost mad by the Nou Camp side in his spell at Madrid, then suggesting finishing second to City at Manchester United was the equivalent of winning the league.

It was similar to Roger Black’s comment at the 1996 Olympics, after taking silver behind Michael Johnson.



He conceded: “You can’t do better than be the best human running against Superman.”

And Guardiola is a managerial Superman. Although nobody has yet discovered the Kryptonite that might take him down.

Of all the rivals, perhaps, Ancelotti has the biggest claim.

Indeed, Don Carlo has achieved some feats so far beyond Pep – winning the title in all the “Big Five” European leagues and a record five Champions League triumphs.

Ancelotti is, though, more of a man manager than an obsessive coach.



The former Milan, PSG, Chelsea, Madrid and Bayern boss, now in charge at Brazil, works by making his players believe they are in charge, even though he is pulling the strings.

Nobody would ever claim that the players run the show under Pep – a man who forced Munich to part company with Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wolfhardt, the leading sports doctor of his age, when they clashed over the fitness of stars to go on the pitch.

With Pep, it is not that every match counts. It is that every training session, every pass, every moment matters totally.

He does not believe it is possible to “complete” football.



There will always be room for refinements and improvements, a man who will not settle until his side has achieved 100 per cent possession in a game, even if that is impossible – as the other team has to kick off at least once and then after every goal conceded.

Yes, Pep has been the beneficiary of being at clubs with in-built advantages.

Spain has been a two-club league for more than half a century, Munich have more cash than the rest of German football put together – even once bailing out Dortmund to prevent their biggest rivals going bust – while City are the global manifestation of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi.

But plenty of others have failed to make the most of their happy inheritance. Pep has used it as a platform for domination. His departure from City will bring a sigh of relief from every other top flight manager.



So what next? Those Ancelotti numbers, probably.

That means France – but that can only be PSG and not before Luis Enrique moves on – or Italy, basically Juventus or Inter Milan, with Paris the obvious preferred option when it comes to adding the extra two Champions League wins.

Or, perhaps, international football. The FA would bend over backwards to have Guardiola in the Wembley dugout five or six times every year, rather than the two or three that has become the norm in his City days.

As a proud Catalan, maybe not Spain. But, after Ancelotti leaves, maybe Brazil?

Whatever he chooses, the fans of his next club, or country, will be beyond excited. There are not supposed to be short cuts to success. Getting Guardiola’s signature, though, is the nearest thing to a guarantee.



Relentless, restless, remarkable. Like Muhammad Ali, The Greatest.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson ‘would have drop kicked’ Mo Salah for bombshell statement swiping at Arne Slot, claims Paul Scholes
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED legend Paul Scholes said Sir Alex Ferguson would have “drop-kicked” Mohamed Salah if he was manager following the Egyptian’s latest swipe at Arne Slot.

Scholes and ex-team-mate Nicky Butt reacted to Salah‘s damning post on X which urged Liverpool to return to “heavy metal football” on their podcast – The Good The Bad & The Football.





Scholes began by saying legendary manager Ferguson would not have stood for Salah’s behaviour and would “drop-kick” the Egyptian if he was in charge.

He believes Salah wouldn’t have even done it if he was playing under Ferguson, who was well-known for his no-nonsense approach.

Scholes also said: “Salah’s a great player, we all love him as a player, but to do something like that when your manager is really struggling.

“He’s [Salah] had a terrible season so what these big players do, they deflect, they will never admit to it being their fault, they blame everybody but themselves.”



The three-time PFA Player of the Year has scored just seven goals this campaign – his worst ever season in a Liverpool shirt.

And with pressure growing on Slot, Butt said he thinks Salah is using his manager as a scapegoat: “There’s a reason why he’s [Salah] doing that it’s because he doesn’t like the bloke [Slot] and he wants him out of the football club.”

Scholes and Butt’s fellow Class of 92 member Gary Neville also weighed in on Salah’s antics, saying he would be “fuming” if a Manchester United player behaved in such a way.

He said: “He’s pulled the pin out of the grenade there, hasn’t he? And just thrown it in the middle of the room.



“I mean, he’s on his way out of the room by the way.”

And another United legend, Wayne Rooney, joined the list of players to slam Salah – saying Slot should bench him in his final game for the club.

On his show he said: “If I was Arne Slot, I’d have him nowhere near the stadium in the last game.”

Salah announced he was leaving the club in an emotional video in March and seems to have had enough at Liverpool.



He hit out at his manager following the Reds’ 4-2 loss to Aston Villa.

Slot’s side are still not confirmed to be playing Champions League football next season with just one game to go.

Sports.title: Tottenham star spotted on the other side of the world barely 24 hours before relegation D-Day clash at Chelsea
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM star Cristian Romero was spotted in Argentina just before his team’s crunch Premier League relegation clash against Chelsea.

Spurs can confirm Prem safety with just a point at Stamford Bridge thanks to their vastly-superior goal difference over 18th-placed West Ham.





But the North Londoners will be without Romero, 28, who has been sidelined for the rest of the season due to a knee injury he suffered last month.

However, the centre-back will also not be present on the bench or the Chelsea stands as he jetted off to his homeland with his wife and two kids via private jet.

The Argentina international shared pictures of him and his family boarding the plane on Instagram without disclosing the destination.

However, Romero recently revealed on social media that he will be present for his hometown club Belgrano’s massive league final against River Plate on Sunday at the Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium.

And reports suggest the defender is already in Cordoba, where the big match will be staged.

This comes after the ex-Atalanta star was pictured passionately celebrating Mathys Tel’s opener during last week’s draw against Leeds along with other injured players.

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi said: “Cristian Romero is a big player, you know he is a big player, but he is an amazing guy because he has been a great captain in my time even though he didn’t play.

“We are talking by phone and when he stay here, every morning he came in my office and he was inside of the season.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

This also comes after De Zerbi didn’t rule out Romero potentially coming back from injury before the end of the season.

The Argentine recently teased a possible return to fitness when he put up a video on social media showing him sprinting on the training pitches.

De Zerbi added: “I don’t know [if Romero will play again before the end of the season], but listen, we have to play another two games.

“Now for our injured players when are they available after a long time with injury? It is a big problem because the season is tough and only one target we have now.

“Play with Romero? Play with [Guglielmo] Vicario? Play with [Antonin] Kinsky?



“The target is just one and to stay up and make point tomorrow [tonight] because this is the target for everyone. Individual targets now are not important.”

But De Zerbi remained coy about Romero’s future at Tottenham with rumours suggesting he will leave this summer amid Atletico Madrid’s persistent interest.

However, the Italian tactician hinted that a lot depends on what the ex-Belgrano star wants to do.

And no concrete decisions will be made before Sunday’s season finale against Everton at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

De Zerbi said: “It is a good question but it is the wrong timing, no? First of all now the focus is Chelsea.

“Second point, Romero is a great player and the most important is the behaviour and how much the player wants to stay in this club.

“We are going to take all the decisions after this season and after the Everton game.”

Sports.title: Burnley co-owner and NFL icon JJ Watt’s brutal tweet slamming Arsenal star Kai Havertz avoiding red for horror tackle
Sports.content:
BURNLEY co-owner and NFL legend J. J. Watt blasted Arsenal star Kai Havertz after the German escaped a red card at the Emirates.

Havertz avoided a sending off during the Gunners’ nervy 1-0 win over Burnley despite a horror challenge that left fans and pundits stunned.





The victory could prove massive for Arsenal in the Premier League title race with Manchester City playing catch up.

Mikel Arteta’s side now know they simply need to beat Crystal Palace in their final game of the season to be crowned Premier League champions for the first time since the Invincibles era in 2004.

It was Havertz who proved the matchwinner against relegated Burnley, powering home a header from a pinpoint Bukayo Saka corner in the first half.

But the Germany international almost went from hero to zero after the break.

Havertz lunged into a late challenge on Burnley midfielder Lesley Ugochukwu, catching him high with his studs in an incident that immediately sparked fury among fans and pundits alike.

Referee Paul Tierney showed Havertz a yellow card, while VAR chose not to send the official to the monitor for an on-field review.

The decision left supporters stunned on social media and Burnley co-owner Watt was among those unimpressed.

Watt posted on X with two images, one of the tackle on Ugochukwu and the other that had the captio of “checking club badge’



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The former Houston Texans superstar has become well known for publicly defending Burnley since investing in the club alongside his wife Kealia in 2023.

Sky Sports commentator Gary Neville was also shocked Havertz stayed on the pitch.

He said: “Vicious from Havertz. He is miles away from the ball. I don’t like that.”

Neville later added: “I don’t think that is right. He is a lucky boy.”



Despite the controversy, Arsenal held on for a crucial victory to keep their title dream alive heading into the final weekend.

Sports.title: Chelsea files: Alonso ‘manager’ tag raises Pochettino questions, classy Joao Pedro moment and youth champions’ dilemma
Sports.content:
A HIGHLY-RATED young coach looking to bounce back from a bruising experience at a big club?

Chelsea have been here before under the current owners.





Mauricio Pochettino will be looking at the appointment of Xabi Alonso with a wry smile.

As well as feeling a sense of vindication, because those in charge at Stamford Bridge seem to have recognised the validity of his recent criticism of how the club was being run.

Poch won the league and cup in France in a season and a half with Paris Saint-Germain.

But it wasn’t enough for the club’s ambitious owners and, after a year licking his wounds, he became the third Blues boss of the BlueCo era in 2023.



Chelsea had just finished 12th in the Premier League after a turbulent season of two “permanent” head coaches, one interim and one caretaker. Which sounds familiar.

The former Tottenham and Southampton head coach took the Blues up to sixth and back into Europe, as well as to the Carabao Cup final and FA Cup semis.

In a recent interview on Gary Neville’s The Overlap podcast, Pochettino said he and his backroom staff thought they had made good progress.

But some in the Chelsea hierarchy disagreed, so on Poch’s account, he decided to leave.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Chelsea Blueprint on YouTube Calling all Chelsea fans - we have a brand new YouTube channel! The Sun’s Chelsea YouTube channel will be your go-to destination for the latest news, transfer updates, match previews, post-match analysis, exclusive interviews, fan reactions, and breaking stories from Stamford Bridge. Subscribe to The Chelsea Blueprint on YouTube now

Central to his belief that things would not work out was the lack of influence he felt he had in recruitment.

He told Neville: “It’s more about a philosophical idea, that the coach and the coaching staff need to be involved in these types of decisions, need to be an important part of the decisions.

“I don’t want to say things that are so obvious, but Manchester City works because Pep is involved in all the things.

“That’s so important.

“The coach cannot be in the corner and say, ‘yes, you only coach the team’, because there are too many things that are going on.



“For players to perform, they need to be attached to the coaches. If not, it’s difficult.

“You need to connect emotionally, the players with the coaches.

“After us it was more clear the idea, the man-management of the club.”

What Poch meant was, it became clear Chelsea wanted head coaches who would accept a limited say in transfers and other areas of the club.



Enzo Maresca played along for a season but then began rebelling and there was a parting of the ways. Liam Rosenior was literally more of a company man, after working under BlueCo at Strasbourg, but could not improve results.

And so now Chelsea have gone back to appointing one of the top coaches in the world.

Only this time they are going to call him – Alonso – a “manager”.

Actions speak louder than words, but the message coming out of the club is there will be greater collaboration between the senior leadership team and owners, and the person in charge of the first team.

Not only in recruitment, but in every area of the club, in an attempt to build a culture which will underpin consistent success.



In other words – or in Poch’s words about Guardiola – “involved in all the things”.

More like Guardiola at City or Mikel Arteta at Arsenal, who does have the title “first-team manager”.

Quite how much power Alonso has, and what he does with it, will be fascinating.

Leading Bayer Leverkusen to their first German title in defiance of the Bayern Munich monopoly was an incredible achievement.

Certainly bigger than Pochettino making PSG French champions again in 2022 – and then not having his contract extended



But Poch came to Chelsea with six and half years of experience in the Premier League.

Alonso has none, and his five years playing here for Liverpool, which ended in 2009, will only help him so much.

Pochettino told Neville the only Chelsea transfers he had a say in were the signings of Axel Disasi and Cole Palmer.

That was not a complaint, just a fact – by the time he arrived, the Blues had already set up most of their business.

Poch may not have hand-picked his squad, but at least Chelsea were in a position to spend more than £400m on players that summer.



They will not be able to do that in the next window. Even if they do cash in on one or more stars like Enzo Fernandez.

They should not need to, either, after splashing out well over £1billion on players since the May 2022 takeover.

But Alonso will want reinforcements and it will be a test of his authority – and the competence of Chelsea’s recruitment department – whether he gets the ones he wants.

And here’s one other similarity between the Spaniard and his Argentina predecessor.

Alonso was fired in January after just months in charge at Real Madrid allegedly because of a breakdown in his relationship with superstar players like Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr.



Earlier this year Pochettino reflected on his time at PSG where, he said, Lionel Messi, Neymar and Mbappe – him again – seemed “bigger than the club itself”.

Poch went on to insist the trio never lacked respect or discipline. But there were definitely problems in the dressing room, with claims of a split between Spanish speakers and French speaking players.

The current Chelsea squad cannot match that PSG group or the current Real crop for egos.

But there are some big personalities (and mouths) like Fernandez and Marc Cucurella to bring into line, and a sense of a return to the days when Blues players could determine the future of a manager by their willingness (or not) to put in maximum effort.

Alonso will have more power than Pochettino, but can he be successful long-term?



And if Poch had stayed and been given a manager role like Alonso’s, would Chelsea be better off than they are now?

JOAO ABOUT THAT?

CHELSEA have announced their men’s player of the season, but he’s not going to the World Cup in the summer.



Joao Pedro won the award, voted for by fans, after his spectacular season up front for the Blues with more than 60 per cent of the votes.

But, he has still not been enough for Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil set-up.

He’s not alone either, with fellow Brazilian’s Estevao and Andrey Santos also both missing out on the 26-man squad.

Andrey Santos wasn’t selected, with Casemiro and others preferred, while Estevao’s absence has allowed for the inclusion of Neymar, who will presumably play his last World Cup for the Selecao.

Brentford‘s Igor Thiago and Lyon‘s Endrick have both been included ahead of him.



Pedro, 24, has been linked with a move to Barcelona this summer, but is considered not for sale by anyone at Chelsea after his 20 goals and nine assists this season – he too is happy in the Premier League with his Brazilian pals.

On Instagram, he said, “I tried to give my best at all times. Unfortunately, it wasn’t possible to fulfil this dream of representing my country in a World Cup, but I remain calm and focused, as I always try to be.

“Joys and frustrations are part of football.

“From now on, I wish good luck to everyone who is there, and I will be just another fan cheering for them to bring the sixth title.”

On the plus side for Chelsea, a summer of rest for their main striker going into next season could be a big boost.



YOUTH SUCCESS

AMONG the items in Xabi Alonso’s in-tray, which few have mentioned, is: what to do with the champions in Chelsea’s youth ranks?

The Under-21 side won PL2 in the regular season, before losing in the play-off quarter finals to Spurs.



The Under-18s finished top of the southern section of the Premier League, and will take on northern kings Manchester City in the national final at Stamford Bridge on Friday night.

Chelsea’s Academy technical director Glenn van der Kraan joined the club in 2024 from City, where he was head of coaching in the youth set-up.

Friday is a chance for revenge for the Blues’ U18s after losing at home last autumn in the FA Youth Cup to City, who went on to win the competition by beating neighbours Manchester United in last week’s final.

The relationship between Alonso’s first team and the talent pathway will be interesting.

There have been noticeably fewer debuts and minutes for teenagers (except Estevao) this season, compared to the opportunities provided by the Conference League in 2024-5.



And Stamford Bridge supremo Behdad Eghbali’s pledge to recruit more “ready-made” players suggests competition will remain fierce next season.

A return to the Conference League might be the best hope of first-team action for the young players. But some well-chosen loans could be the best option for the likes of prolific striker Shim Mheuka.

UEFA RULES



EVEN if Chelsea do not qualify for Europe next season, they will have to continue to abide by the terms of their four-year settlement agreement with Uefa.

Which sounds obvious, but the reality has been lost in all the debate about whether the Blues should hold their hands up and trigger a year-long ban from Uefa competition if they do make it into the Conference League or Europa League.

Rather than risk breaching the terms of the deal further down the line and risk missing out on a place in the much more lucrative Champions League.

The terms of the deal with the European governing body after the club broke financial rules set annual limits on losses, but also involve a rolling three-year assessment period.

The club insists it is confident of abiding by all relevant financial regulations at domestic and continental level.



But if Chelsea do miss out on European football altogether, they would be given more leeway under the Premier League’s new squad cost ratio regulations.

Teams competing in Europe have to abide by Uefa’s limit of spending no more than 70 per cent of their football income on wages, amortisation and agent fees. But PL sides without continental obligations are allowed 85 per cent.

Even allowing for other differences between the two sets of regulations, it is hard to see how Chelsea could take advantage of that 15 per cent for one season and stay in Uefa’s good books.

Although, given the BlueCo regime’s previous financial creativity, you never know.

FEELING FIT, LADS?



A NEW manager can sometimes mean a tough new regime for players – and fitness coaches are often the most feared.

However, in Xabi Alonso’s case, the Chelsea squad could be exposed to something rather new.

Ismael Camenforte Lopez, who worked at Barcelona’s famed La Masia academy for seven years, is one of four coaches Alonso will bring to West London with him.

The fitness coach, who became part of his staff at Bayer Leverkusen having previously been head of methodology at the club, has been praised for his progressive methods.

Camenforte has been noticed for his high level of tactical awareness as a fitness coach, often involving a ball and re-creating match situations to keep players engaged.



So while the Blues squad may not be pushed beyond their limits by an old-school fitness coach keen on punishment, they will certainly be getting a mental working out on top of any tired legs.

MM IS AT IT AGAIN

CHELSEA’s ‘Moroccan Messi’ is tearing it up at the u17 AFCON.



Ibrahim Rabbaj is highly rated by fans and people internally at Chelsea alike.

He has completed more dribbles than any other player in the competition so far, and was given the player of the match award in his first game in the tournament.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He has been linked with a move also to Barcelona, after spending some time in La Masia as a child as well as at Crystal Palace.

Rabbaj, though, is under contract with Chelsea until 2028.

Sports.title: How Pep Guardiola changed English football forever from tiki-taka to fashionista wearing rollnecks and hoodies
Sports.content:
LONG after Pep Guardiola has gone, his impact on English football will still be felt.

Arriving in the Premier League ten years ago as one of the great minds in the game’s history, his style was derided even if his achievements at Barcelona and Bayern Munich were not.





Could he do it on a wet Tuesday night in Stoke, was the question.

Is a man who had fallen short in Europe with a Bayern mega-team really suitable for ‘Our League’?

Does Pep just rely on having the biggest access to club bank balances and the best players?

How would his Tiki-Taka possession plan work against the physicality in this country?

As it turns out, pretty well.

He will depart Manchester City as a six-time Prem winner – at least.

That could still become seven depending on what happens in the final week of the season.

Either way, his legacy will hardly be dented if Arsenal do take what has so often been Pep’s crown.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Guardiola – labelled a bald fraud and a serial overthinker – has picked up 15 major trophies in his time at the Etihad.

There are three Community Shields, a Club World Cup, and a Uefa Super Cup to pad out his collection.

But it has never been just about the silverware with Pep.



He is one of the sport’s most lovingly confusing characters – so pent up with energy he can ramble on to a room without making much sense but engrossing it nonetheless.

His success goes beyond just the many wins. It is embedded into the very foundation of the game in England now.

Crawley will play from the back, splitting centre-halves and actively look to exploit overloads in all phases.

Goalkeepers will pass into danger rather than play safe. The best way to be a midfielder is to start as a full-back.

Kids are growing up with these roles more defined than ever. The level of tactical complexity has soared.



It feels as though English football as a whole thinks about the game more than ever – so much so that Pep was considered and reportedly offered the national team job.

And yes, going hairless without a beard is still a big fashion statement.

So what are the five biggest ways Guardiola has fundamentally altered the landscape of English football, and how will it hold up over time?



The death of Brexitball and birth of Tiki-Taka

Guardiola actually doesn’t like the phrase Tiki-Taka because it implies possession for the sake of possession – something he hates and doesn’t like to be associated with. Everything has a purpose.

Instead, he has been focused on control. Force opponents deep with “a thousand, million passes,” and penning them in.

The counter- press suffocates – attack, or possession, as the best form of defence – and then relentless overloads are exploited.

Guardiola’s form of Juego de Posicion (JdP, positional play) was a world away from hoofing long balls in a 4-4-2.

None of the Sam Allardyce “good old- fashioned” physical brutality with massive bruisers up front, lumping it long to the big man, winning knockdowns to the little man, and going from there.



Pep’s methodical football changed how most view the game.

Although the past few years and a reversion to set pieces, long throws, and even a Tony Pulis-like four centre-backs starting – with two at full-back – have not stopped Pep’s ultimate aims.

You will see children playing possession ball, rondos and taking more risks than ever to try and emulate the style that led Pep to total dominance.

Redefining player roles

It is long forgotten now, but in an age of wingers cutting in and firing it into the top corner – Franck Ribéry and Arjen Robben at his lethal Bayern Munich side – Pep reverted to out-and-out wide men.

The left footed Leroy Sane played on the left and Raheem Sterling was on the right.



Pep used cut-backs and back-post crosses to exploit gaps in-behind a defence, going against the grain.

When struggling in 2022, he moved Joao Cancelo into midfield to find a new way of building in possession to his preferred 3-2-5 shape.

Before long, Rico Lewis was maybe the first specialist player in this hybrid position.

It has been a much more popular thing ever since.

Even John Stones was deployed as a No10 at times.



Before Pep, it is hard to imagine anything like this happening as regularly across the game from Prem competitors to grassroots.

Evolving the goalkeeper

Joe Hart was probably City’s best-ever goalkeeper before Pep came along.

He dropped him immediately in favour of a ball-playing specialist.



Now, the arrival of Claudio Bravo hardly worked, but it signalled the shift to having players comfortable in possession across the field.

The demand for passing and possession mastery went beyond what many saw as the usually desired skillset for most positions.

Again, this season – with Erling Haaland at one end and Gianluigi Donnarumma at the other – is a bit of an outlier, but also evidence of his further adaption.

But at the start, Pep’s use of goalies, not as a defensive tool or final barrier, was radical.

Excellent shot-stopper Hart was binned – and never really recovered.



And that was just the first of his many ploys.

Ederson took things to a new level with claims that he could actually have been used in midfield or was the team’s best penalty- taker.

He became established as the new norm of GKs after Pep changed the way they were seen.



Setting new standards of excellence

When Pep arrived, Jose Mourinho‘s 95-point Prem record stood alone and had done for 15 years.

Nobody had scored more than Carlo Ancelotti‘s Chelsea in 2009-10 (103) either.

It took him a year to figure out, but when Pep got going in 2017-18, nobody could stop him.

City smashed the points record, becoming the first – and so far only – team to reach three figures in a league campaign.

They banged in 106 goals that season as well, shattering expectations.



When Liverpool got 97 points the year after, it would have won them all but one Prem title in history.

Guardiola’s City pipped them with 98, going on a run of 14 straight wins – that extended back to 18/19 in the second half of the season.

These surges to the title became a habit.

Guardiola fought off Jurgen Klopp‘s Liverpool and set new highs against Mikel Arteta and Arsenal as well.

They won four in a row, something not even the great Sir Alex Ferguson achieved.



Pep’s side completed a historic first domestic treble. And they did it with the Champions League in 2023 to rob neighbours United of their unique bragging rights.

Modernising the touchline fashionista

Pep is also an unexpected fashion icon.

Far from the suit and trousers he would rock in the early days, or the grey trousers from Barca, he is now a trend setter.



City’s clothing range leaves him with a giant letter P on current jumpers and jackets.

He will regularly wear Stone Island gear, more often seen in the stands than pitchside.

Stories were written about his famous grey cardigan that cost thousands of pounds, or a Roberto Mancini-like scarf era.

Pep’s smart-casual luxury outfit choice has become a talking point for fans as much as his football.

He will pace the technical area in a slick rollneck and sharp white trainers where others only sport tracksuits.



There is nothing bland about Pep, who is not afraid to show off big-name brands, popular logos, or out-there fashion design.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A role model and catwalk model in one. Touchline fashion is all the rage and Pep was never going to miss out.

You might not see Sunday league managers donning cargoes or brightly coloured footwear like Guardiola, but his impact goes way beyond the naked eye anyway.

Sports.title: Arsenal sweating on Jurrien Timber injury as Mikel Arteta gets worrying update
Sports.content:
Arsenal sweating on Jurrien Timber injury as Mikel Arteta gets worrying update

Arsenal are facing up to the prospect of facing Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final without a specialised right-back with Jurrien Timber and Ben White both injured

View 3 Images Jurrien Timber could miss the Champions League final (Image: Photo by Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Jurrien Timber's chances of being fit for the Champions League final “do not look rosy.”

‌



That comes despite the Arsenal defender stepping up his training this week in a desperate bid to be ready for the showdown with Paris Saint Germain on May 30 and the World Cup. Timber has been out since mid-March with a groin injury and has already seen attempted comebacks suffer setbacks.

‌



But the Holland full-back is understood to be more confident this time despite his own national manager, Ronald Koeman, fearful that he could be left without a key player.

‌



Koeman, who will name his World Cup squad on May 27, said: “Jurrien has been dealing with this for quite some time. It has been on and off.

Ex-Premier League referee gives Arsenal immediate Kai Havertz red card verdict READ MORE :

Furious Pep Guardiola summons Man City stars in late-night summit to confirm exit READ MORE :

“He is now training up again to see if he can make the Champions League final and if he is available for the World Cup. It does not look rosy at the moment.”

The hope is that Timber will step up his training work this week and even join the first team group ahead of Sunday’s final Premier League game of the season at Crystal Palace. He would be highly unlikely to be ready for that but Arsenal face a PSG side in Budapest that boasts winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia who is regarded as one of the best in the world.

‌



It would be a big gamble but they are already without Ben White and would have to otherwise use centre half Cristhian Mosquera as a makeshift right back.

That is why Arsenal are keen to get Timber back to speed in the hope of him having a chance but if he does not make it then he will miss the World Cup and could even need surgery on the issue.

Timber's absence would be another setback for Koeman. Defender Matthijs de Ligt, midfielder Jerdy Schouten, and forward Xavi Simons are already out through injury.

‌



View 3 Images Timber hasn't featured for Arsenal since March (Image: Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Mikel Merino is another Arsenal player hoping to be back into full training ahead of the Champions League after foot surgery. The Gunners midfielder has been out for four months and is set to miss the World Cup but has stepped up his training in the past week.

He admitted that it has been very difficult to watch from the sidelines and has “suffered” at times with the fans while he is even harder to put up with when he watches at home on TV with his new baby.

‌



Merino said: “It’s hard because on the one hand I want to be on the pitch supporting my teammates because I was born to play football

“But if you cannot do it, you have to do it in a different way and make an impact and my role is to give advice, give tips and support in the bad times as well.

“I try to push for my position now and make everyone put a bit on the table now so we can win a trophy at the end of the season.

‌



“If I’m in the stadium then I’m quite quiet but if I’m at home then I shout at the TV which is not great with the baby sleeping next to me!

“But I suffer, you can feel stressed like everyone else. When you’re on the pitch you don’t feel that pressure, you don’t feel it so much and you just want to be out there.”

View 3 Images Mikel Merino is another player currently sidelined (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Merino insisted that despite missing a chunk of the season that he is still living the dream and has enjoyed coming into training.

He added: “It’s a dream to be honest, what you dream of as a kid and you can win the title, the Champions League, they are the things you can only dream of and now you are living them right now.

“I feel blessed, it’s a huge opportunity and I’m enjoying being round these people.

‌



“It’s only been two seasons but I feel like I’ve been here for a long, long time and I feel part of the family for sure.

“It’s great going to work every day, you work hard, it’s tough but when you’re in the physio room, when you’re in the gym, you have good banter.

“We have an amazing squad and it’s time to use it and get to the final stages of the season with good vibes.”

Sports.title: Arsenal fans shell out £10,000 for vital Crystal Palace tie to see Gunners lift Premier League trophy
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Arsenal fans shell out £10,000 for vital Crystal Palace tie to see Gunners lift Premier League trophy

Money appears to be no obstacle for Gunners followers desperate to see captain Martin Odegaard lift the trophy. The match in south London is a 25,000 sell-out but tickets are changing hands for huge sums on online resale sites

View 4 Images Arsenal beat Burnley 1-0 at home to edge closer to the title

Arsenal fans are forking out more than £10,000 for the chance to see their team lift the Premier League trophy.

‌



Touts are charging eye-watering sums for the Gunners’ final match of the season at Crystal Palace on Sunday. Arsenal are currently five points ahead of nearest rivals manchester-city-fc>Manchester City.

‌



Pep Guardiola's men need to win at Bournemouth tonight to take the title race to the final day. If Arsenal beat Palace at Selhurst Park they will be crowned champions for the first time since 2004.

‌



Money appears to be no obstacle for Gunners followers desperate to see captain Martin Odegaard lift the trophy. The match in south London is a 25,000 sell-out but tickets are changing hands for huge sums on online resale sites.

View 4 Images Arsenal could win the Premier League title as early as tonight (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Furious Pep Guardiola summons Man City stars in late-night summit to confirm exit READ MORE :

Ex-Premier League referee gives Arsenal immediate Kai Havertz red card verdict READ MORE :

One site - livefootballtickets.com - is selling away end tickets for over £33,000. Another site - Ticombo.com - has seen Arsenal fans pay over £10,000 for a seat in the visitors’ section. The cheapest tickets available online are selling for £1,300 in the home sections.

‌



Palace bosses have warned any Arsenal fans found in home sections of the ground will be ejected. The club has also announced “enhanced security measures” for the 4pm kick-off.

Ticket sharing has been disabled and supporters found sharing a ticket face a ban next season. Just over 3,000 tickets have been allocated to Arsenal’s loyal away fans.

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta is close to winning the Premier League title (Image: 2026 Eurasia Sport Images)

‌



The Metropolitan Police is expected to draft in extra officers for the hugely-anticipated game. Ticketless Gunners fans will pack into pubs on Holloway Road and near their Emirates stadium.

Arsene Wenger was the Arsenal manager when they last won the league 22 years ago. Frenchman Thierry Henry, now a Sky TV pundit, finished top scorer with 30 goals.

Many football observers believed Arteta’s men had “bottled” the title after they lost to Bournemouth and Manchester City last month. But they have won all four games since the City defeat - while their rivals dropped two points in a 3-3 draw with Everton.

‌



View 4 Images Arsene Wenger and Patrick Vieira during the Premier League Trophy parade (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Sunday’s match is being billed as the biggest for the Gunners since their 1989 final-day victory over Liverpool. Michael Thomas scored a dramatic injury time winner at Anfield to clinch the title for George Graham’s men.

Arsenal are hoping for a double celebration when they take on Paris St Germain in the Champions League final on May 30. More than 20,000 are expected to travel to Budapest for the game.

Article continues below

Thousands more will watch the match on big screens at the Emirates Stadium.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim set for shock return to management as replacement for another ex-Man Utd boss
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim set for shock return to management as replacement for another ex-Man Utd boss

Ruben Amorim has been out of work since leaving Manchester United back in January but the former Sporting Lisbon boss could soon return to the dugout in familiar surroundings

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim could become Benfica's next head coach (Image: Getty Images)

Ruben Amorim is on the cusp of a return to management after being lined up to replace another former Manchester United manager in Jose Mourinho at Benfica.

‌



Though he arrived in the Premier League with a burgeoning reputation, Amorim endured a turbulent tenure at Old Trafford and the 41-year-old was sacked by the club back in January. The Red Devils fortunes have improved significantly under Michael Carrick, who is poised to become head coach on a permanent basis after impressing in an interim capacity.

‌



Amorim initially made his name as a coach in Portugal with Sporting Lisbon, where he won two Portuguese titles - and his return to management could come at one of their biggest rivals.

‌



The Sun claim Benfica have set their sights on Amorim to succeed Mourinho, who is Real Madrid-bound after agreeing a return to the Spanish giants.

Raging Roy Keane rips into Bruno Fernandes and Man Utd stars' behaviour in explosive rant READ MORE :

Gary Neville names the SIX quality signings Man Utd must make to back Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Though Amorim has strong links with Sporting Lisbon, he did represent Benfica in his playing days and even finished his career at the club before moving into coaching.

He is also 'close friends' with the Benfica president, Rui Costa, who was the club's sporting director during Amorim's playing spell. The Benfica chief is still an avid admirer of Amorim, who won just 25 of his 63 games at Manchester United.

‌



Intriguingly, Amorim was previously touted as a potential successor to Pep Guardiola, who has decided to leave Manchester City at the end of the season after a trophy-laden decade at the helm.

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho is set to complete a sensational return to Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Hugo Viana, the sporting director Amorim worked closely with during his stint at Sporting Lisbon, took up a similar position at The Etihad last year and it was reported that City had identified Amorim as a candidate to replace Guardiola back in October 2024.

‌



Other top clubs were also credited with an interest in Amorim during his time in Portugal including Liverpool.

However, it was Manchester United who moved for the Portuguese coach just weeks after City's interest had been reported after deciding to sack Erik ten Hag.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola is the best manager in Premier League history and an impossible act to follow
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola is the best manager in Premier League history and an impossible act to follow

Pep Guardiola will bring the curtain down on a trophy-laden decade at Manchester City following the Blues' final two games of the Premier League season this week

View 3 Images Pep leaves Man City as the greatest in Premier League history (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola has been the most influential manager of the modern era. And undoubtedly the best. Guardiola has not just won trophies - he has redefined the game, changed how we watch it and changed how we play it.

‌



The Manchester City manager is a pioneer. A legend who, in my opinion, stands above Sir Alex Ferguson, Jose Mourinho and Arsene Wenger. They are the great managers of the Premier League era - and Guardiola has matched them all and more.

‌



Why? Because Guardiola has not only won - 20 trophies in his remarkable 10 years - but has done it with such style.

‌



For those with shorter memories, his first year at City did not go to plan. They did not play how he wanted, he had a nightmare with his keepers - Claudio Bravo could kick but not catch - and he finished third, having just scraped into the Champions League places.

But this is what Pep is all about; he refused to buckle and change his principles. He refused to ditch his style and carried on.

Furious Pep Guardiola summons Man City stars in late-night summit to confirm exit READ MORE :

I remember going to Goodison Park on January 15, 2017, and City were absolutely thumped 4-0 by Everton in a game which will probably go down as Guardiola’s lowest point.

‌



Guardiola looked shell-shocked afterwards. Romelu Lukaku, Kevin Mirallas, Tom Davies and Ademola Lookman scored. City looked clueless.

I came away thinking: Guardiola will never work in the Premier League. How wrong was I? This is the ultimate perfectionist; my way or the highway.

There is a great story from the dressing room from that first season. At Crystal Palace, November 19, 2016, City escaped with a 2-1 win on a difficult day at Selhurst Park. Connor Wickham scored for Palace and Yaya Toure scored twice for City.

‌



The players were expecting congratulations when they came back into the dressing room. Not pretty. But they won. It was tough.

Instead, Guardiola went mad and told them all he would rather lose playing his style and football than win like that. Playing ugly. It could never happen again, he said.

It still took time but the players really understood then. This is the manager who sets standards - and sticks by them.

‌



As a manager, he was defined by Barcelona legend Johan Cruyff. He challenged and teased the Barcelona hierarchy to give the rookie coach the job (he was coaching the B team but his potential was obvious) - and built one of the greatest teams in European football. The rest is history.

View 3 Images Guardiola led City to their first and only Champions League triumph (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Lionel Messi, Xavi, Andres Iniesta and Co conquered and won the lot with incredible style. Arguably the best team of the Champions League era. His team at Bayern Munich was even more pretty - but could not deliver the ultimate prize of the European Cup.

‌



That dogged him at City. He even blew it by overthinking it in the “Covid final” in 2021 against Chelsea when he played without a holding midfielder - and lost.

But Guardiola got there eventually with a historic Treble, four Premier League titles in a row and so many more slices of history.

He is intense, determined and single-minded. A born winner. Players talk about their “heads spinning” with so many instructions, details and stepping into different positions.

‌



They talk about his warmth publicly but that is more likely a desire to please the managerial genius in front of them. One player who has been through it all, is one of their longest-serving stars privately revealed he has had two “proper conversations” with Guardiola in the best part of a decade. Guardiola did not want to be loved. He just wants to win.

Guardiola took playing out from the back to a whole new level. The risk and reward. It was brilliant to watch. The inverted full back - a defender stepping into midfield - seemed to give City an extra man. That was the beauty of his tactics.

In peak Joao Cancelo - he was arguably the best - they just seemed to have 12 players on the pitch. It just was not fair. At the Club World Cup last summer, he was different. This was a new team. One in transition and still building. He was more relaxed and enjoying it.

‌



He even allowed himself a laugh when he saw a few familiar faces in the press. Coming up, asking after us, a joke, a smile and he enjoyed engaging.

View 3 Images Guardiola will leave City after Sunday's match against Aston Villa (Image: AP Photo/Dave Thompson)

That has carried through into this season. Jokes at press conferences. Even doing the West Ham gesture - Come On You Irons - ahead of their game with title rivals Arsenal. You would have to be blind not to see it. Even after the FA Cup final on Saturday, he made for his security man on the pitch, hugged him, thanked him. He was saying goodbye.

‌



Guardiola has been demob happy because he knew he was going. It is so obvious it has been coming. They have sounded out Enzo Maresca because he is a coach, has great ideas and was at City. But he can never be Pep - and nor should he try to be.

Guardiola is an impossible act to follow. The whisper has been going round for so long that potential new signings back in January even enquired whether Guardiola was staying or not. Well, you would ask, wouldn’t you?

The answer came back with there can be no guarantees. But City would appoint well and if someone new comes in then they will be a top drawer coach.

Article continues below

Sadly, no-one will ever be Pep.

Sports.title: Premier League explain Arsenal red card controversy as Gary Neville says 'it's horrible'
Sports.content:
Premier League explain Arsenal red card controversy as Gary Neville says 'it's horrible'

Kai Havertz was particularly fortunate to avoid a red card in Arsenal's win over Burnley following his tackle on Lesley Ugochukwu, with Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville disagreeing with the outcome

View 2 Images Kai Havertz was shown a yellow card for a bad foul on Lesley Ugochukwu (Image: (Mike Egerton/PA Wire))

Gary Neville believes Arsenal forward Kai Havertz was 'lucky' to avoid a red card for a challenge on Burnley midfielder Lesley Ugochukwu. Havertz lunged into Ugochukwu in the 67th minute as Burnley attempted to drive the ball forward against the Gunners from the edge of their own box.

‌



Havertz's studs appeared to rake down Ugochukwu's calf from behind, with the 22-year-old seemingly indicating he felt the tackle was excessive.

‌



Referee Paul Tierney swiftly produced a yellow card, but Neville, serving as co-commentator for Sky Sports, felt the Germany international should have been given his marching orders.

‌



He said: "I don't like that. I don't like it at all. It's a horrible one, it's vicious from Havertz. I think this is a red. There's no way you're getting the ball, you can only hurt the player there."

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Ex-Premier League referee gives Arsenal immediate Kai Havertz red card verdict READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta's instant reaction to Pep Guardiola quitting Man City as Arsenal boss quizzed READ MORE :

The VAR James Bell reviewed the incident but stuck with Tierney's on-field decision to caution Havertz. Neville responded: "I don't think it's right - he's a lucky boy. I'd get him off the pitch straight away."

‌



Mikel Arteta did subsequently withdraw goalscorer Havertz from the action, with Viktor Gyokeres introduced shortly afterwards.

The Premier League's Match Centre account provided clarification on the ruling, posting on X: "The referee's call of yellow card to Havertz was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the challenge deemed not to be serious foul play."

Arsenal are now just one victory away from securing a first Premier League title in 22 years following a 1-0 triumph over Burnley. The Gunners head to Crystal Palace on the final day, though that win may prove unnecessary should second-placed Manchester City stumble at Bournemouth on Tuesday night (7:30pm BST).

‌



Arteta has urged the club's supporters to play their part, with a Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain also on the horizon.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has called on Arsenal fans to play a big role in their final two season-defining games

Speaking after Monday's win over the Clarets, he said: "It's an absolute joy to witness the transformation and contribution each of you has had to turn this place into the most beautiful place to enjoy a football club.

Article continues below

"This is the soul of this football club. Each of you contribute to that. Make sure every time you step in this stadium, you face the responsibility to keep it at these standards. It makes all the difference.

"I will see you soon in Selhurst Park and then Budapest as well. Please be the protagonists to these amazing group of players and staff."

Sports.title: Who will be in Thomas Tuchel's 26-man England World Cup squad?
Sports.content:
The wait is nearly over. Thomas Tuchel names his 26 man squad for the World Cup on Friday.

And if one player has made a late push for the plane then it has to be Chelsea’s fit-again central defender Levi Colwill.

Having missed so much of the season through a knee injury, his performance in front of Tuchel at Wembley must have caught the England manager’s eye.

Colwill also played so well at Liverpool in his previous game and, if you were judging him just on those two performances, he would be in the squad for his quality, composure and leadership.

‌



England submit provisional World Cup squad - and it could include unlikely wildcard READ MORE :

The versatile centre half - he can play in a back four, part of a back three and as a left back - is a superb defender and also strong personality. He is what Chelsea need long term.

But this is all about fitness and whether he will be ready for a gruelling tournament having just come back from injury.

I think Harry Maguire might miss out, despite a stellar second half of the season. Personally I would take him, but I think Tuchel might be going in a different direction.

That is the dilemma facing Tuchel and he probably has one on both flanks. At right back, Reece James is in pole position. Jarell Quansah is a back-up option. But could he risk Tino Livramento who is an injury worry?

‌



On the left, Nico O’Reilly looks a shoo-in at left back. But then there’s Lewis Hall who has been in and out for Newcastle. Could Tuchel use Dan Burn - who he wants to take - as a left back option? Or even Myles Lewis-Skelly.

England World Cup squad verdict reached as Thomas Tuchel urged to drop big-name star READ MORE :

England will almost certainly take three strikers. That is what Tuchel is planning for in a 26-man squad.

Harry Kane is stitched-on. But then Ollie Watkins was not in March - and yet has been fantastic since then. He must go.

It is a straight choice between Ivan Toney and Danny Welbeck, in my view. I'd be tempted to take Dominic Calvert-Lewin but it is questionable as to whether he passed the audition in March.

‌



These are the questions facing Tuchel this week. He names his squad on Friday. He may add a couple in case of injury as stand-by because the squad does not have to be in until June 1 for FIFA.

FIFA then make it public on June 2.

Do not forget that Tuchel will probably watch through his fingers in the final weekend of the Premier League season. Last minute injuries are such a worry….

Sports.title: Leeds United £20million transfer left in limbo by Southampton Spygate scandal
Sports.content:
Leeds United £20million transfer left in limbo by Southampton Spygate scandal

The outcome of Southampton's Spygate investigation could impact Leeds United's transfer plans

View 2 Images Daniel Farke's transfer plans at Leeds could be impacted (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

The conclusion of Southampton's Spygate inquiry could have significant consequences for Leeds United's transfer ambitions. The Premier League outfit are reportedly eyeing Middlesbrough midfielder Hayden Hackney, with the Championship club believed to be holding out for £20million for his signature.

‌



The 23-year-old is set to enter the final year of his deal. However, any potential transfer could well hinge on the verdict handed down to the Saints, who were charged by the EFL for spying on a Middlesbrough training session just two days before the first leg of their play-off semi-final.

‌



The EFL confirmed that a disciplinary hearing would be held on or before Tuesday, with Tonda Eckert's side currently scheduled to face Hull City in the Wembley play-off final on Saturday.

‌



Having secured their Premier League status earlier this month, Leeds will be eager to strengthen their squad, though their pursuit of Hackney could be impacted by the ruling. Should Middlesbrough be reinstated into the play-offs and go on to win promotion, the club may opt to hold onto their prized asset or slap a considerably heftier price tag on him.

Conversely, if the commission rules in Southampton's favour, Middlesbrough could struggle to retain Hackney and would lose much of their bargaining power, potentially leaving Leeds able to land him for considerably less than the original asking price.

What six pundits say about Spygate and Southampton's potential punishment READ MORE :

Southampton facing points deduction and huge ban for boss Tonda Eckert over Spygate READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Leeds' return to the Premier League has proven a triumph, with the Whites sitting 14th in the table with just one match remaining. Despite appearing to be prime relegation candidates as recently as March, Farke's men have embarked on a remarkable eight-game unbeaten run since that point.

Following a 1-0 victory over Brighton courtesy of Dominic Calvert-Lewin's stoppage-time strike, the German manager addressed supporters directly at Elland Road to praise their unwavering backing.

View 2 Images Southampton are currently scheduled to face Hull City in the Championship play-off final on Saturday (Image: Robin Jones, Getty Images)

‌



He also delivered a pointed message to the club's ownership, setting out his vision for Leeds going forward. Farke said: "This game more or less sums up perfectly our whole season. The mentality, spirit and fight in this dressing room is second to none.

"This is why we can celebrate all together today. So thanks a lot for all your support, it is second to none. Just a final promise - I know we have the best fans in this country, it's second to none.

"Right now we are also working to get one of the best teams in this country. Thanks a lot." Leeds end their season on Sunday away to West Ham, whose relegation could be confirmed if Tottenham defeat Chelsea on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: Raducanu suffers defeat on clay in first match since March
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu suffered a 6-4 7-6 (7-4) defeat to Diane Parry of France in her first clay tournament of 2026 at the Internationaux de Strasbourg on Tuesday.

Raducanu was making her return to the WTA Tour after missing more than two months with a post-viral illness.

The former US Open champion accepted a replacement spot in the WTA 500 event, and she was joined by Andrew Richardson after reappointing the US Open-winning coach.

Parry headed into the clash with Raducanu having clinched the Clarins WTA 125 in Paris on Sunday after her opponent Madison Keys was unable to continue the final despite winning the first set.

Wearing heavy strapping on her left thigh, the French No 4 appeared fatigued from her travels, compared to her opponent, who was playing her first match since a thrashing at the hands of Amanda Anisimova at Indian Wells.

Raducanu, who has slipped to 37th in the rankings, looked sharp with her movement and received an early tonic by breaking for a 4-2 lead in the opening set.

But the British No 1 yielded her advantage in the next game, and with the court drying out after an early start in Strasbourg, a third double fault from Raducanu followed by a thumping Parry forehand secured a third consecutive break, but more importantly it gave the Frenchwomen a chance to serve for the set.

World No 94 Parry snuffed out a couple of break points for Raducanu, and urged on by her home fans, she sealed the set in 56 minutes of a fluctuating back-and-forth clash.

Image: Andrew Richardson is back coaching Raducanu, nearly five years since he guided her to the US Open title

Raducanu regathered her thoughts to compose herself and pounce for a 4-2 advantage, but in a mirror image of the opening set the 23-year-old gifted Parry an immediate break back.

The double faults were mounting up for Raducanu and an eighth followed by a wild forehand gave Parry an opportunity to serve it out, but a superb return game denied the Frenchwoman as the Briton drew level at 5-5.

They traded service breaks once again in a match of intense drama, as the contest headed into a tie-break.

Despite a valiant effort from Raducanu, it was Parry who capitalised on a couple of errors to seal the win and avenge her defeat to the Brit in a Billie Jean King Cup qualifying rubber in 2024.

Raducanu will now head into the French Open, which begins on May 24, with only one clay-court match under her belt.

Henman: Raducanu coaching change comes at perfect time

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Both Tim Henman and Laura Robson believe Raducanu reuniting with Andrew Richardson is a good move

Former British No 1 Tim Henman recently backed Raducanu's decision to reappoint Richardson ahead of a huge summer of tennis.

Raducanu was strongly criticised for axing Richardson shortly after her stunning win in New York in 2021. At the time, the now 23-year-old said she felt she needed someone with WTA Tour experience, but, nearly five years and a host of short-term appointments later, Raducanu has again turned to Richardson.

"Grateful to have reconnected with someone who has known me for over a decade now and looking forward to building together one iteration at a time," said Raducanu.

It continues a pattern of Raducanu favouring coaches who she worked with prior to her rapid ascent to superstardom - a decision that four-time Wimbledon semi-finalist Henman views as the right call.

"I think it's great that Andrew is back to support Emma and all I can say is I hope it lasts a bit longer," Henman said on Sky Sports.

"They had an incredible run in America all those years ago and it stopped working after that. She's been through a lot of other coaches between now and then.

"They obviously have a relationship from the past - Emma obviously trusts Andrew - and I think that consistency and continuity is really important, especially at this time of year.

"She's got the French Open coming up, but then the grass-court season, where the spotlight is going to be at its most intense - pre-Wimbledon and at Wimbledon."

Former British No 1 Laura Robson feels Raducanu's decision to reunite with Richardson will help her feel more relaxed knowing a "familiar voice".

She said: "At this stage she's trying to come back from a long-term illness over the last couple of months, so to come back with a familiar voice, someone who you trust already, someone who you've been through so much with, probably feels quite relaxing in a way.

"To have the same ideas of what they're trying to do with her game on the court makes a big difference. Clearly it's worked in the past so why not give it round two?"

Sports.title: England captain Sciver-Brunt in race to be fit for Women's T20 World Cup
Sports.content:
England captain Nat Sciver-Brunt is in a fitness race against time for next month's T20 World Cup, having been ruled out of series against New Zealand and India.

The 33-year-old suffered a calf tear playing for The Blaze against Warwickshire on April 29, and the ECB confirmed on Tuesday that a longer period of rehabilitation will now be needed for the injury.

England and New Zealand meet in three T20 internationals starting in Derby on May 20, ahead of further games at Canterbury (May 23) and Hove (May 25).

They will then play three T20 internationals versus India before beginning their home T20 World Cup campaign against Sri Lanka at Edgbaston on Friday June 12.

Sciver-Brunt is now confirmed as missing all six of the contests before the World Cup.

Image: Sciver-Brunt first injured her calf on April 29 playing for The Blaze against Warwickshire

"Nat Sciver-Brunt has been ruled out of both Vitality IT20 series against New Zealand and India," an ECB statement read.

"Sciver-Brunt is still recovering from a tear in her left calf. Following a scan on Monday, England Women have confirmed a longer period of rehabilitation is needed to enable Sciver-Brunt to play a full part in the upcoming ICC Women's T20 World Cup."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights from the first innings of the third ODI between England and New Zealand.

England have not won the T20 World Cup since the inaugural edition on home soil in 2009 and were knocked out in the group stage at the last edition, in the UAE in 2024.

New Zealand are the reigning Women's T20 World Cup champions, claiming a first title two years ago with a 32-run victory over South Africa in the Dubai final.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England lose the wickets of Freya Kemp, Alice Capsey and Dani Gibson in quick succession during their third ODI with New Zealand in Cardiff.

Elsewhere, Danni Wyatt-Hodge will also miss the New Zealand series with the birth of her first child imminent, while England Women have called up Hampshire's Maia Bouchier and Warwickshire's Charis Pavely to the T20 squad for the New Zealand series as cover.

Sports.title: 43-year-old Gordon plus Curtis and Stewart named in Scotland's World Cup squad
Sports.content:
Scotland head coach Steve Clarke has named Craig Gordon, Findlay Curtis and Ross Stewart in his 26-man squad for the World Cup.

Hearts goalkeeper Gordon, 43, missed out on the last Euros but takes his place alongside Angus Gunn of Nottingham Forest and Liam Kelly of Rangers - despite the trio not featuring regularly at club level this season.

Scotland goalkeepers: Club appearances this season Craig Gordon (Hearts) - 3

Liam Kelly (Rangers) - 3

Angus Gunn (Nottingham Forest) - 1

Clarke has shown loyalty throughout his tenure and that remains with this group. Eight defenders and seven midfielders who featured in every qualification group are in.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at how Scotland revealed their first World Cup squad in 28 years. Credit: @ScotlandNT

In the back-line that includes some of those you'd expect, like captain Andy Robertson, Celtic's Kieran Tierney and Aaron Hickey of Brentford, there's also room for Celtic's Anthony Ralston, Rangers' John Souttar and Grant Hanley of Hibernian, who was a fitness doubt.

Then you've got midfielder Scott McTominay, who scored that overhead kick against Denmark, alongside the likes of John McGinn, Ben Gannon-Doak and Kenny McLean, yes the one who scored from the halfway line.

Image: Scott McTominay's incredible bicycle kick helped Scotland beat Denmark to secure a spot at the World Cup

There is also a spot for Bologna's Lewis Ferguson, and Curtis, who has been rewarded for an impressive end to the season on loan at Kilmarnock.

The Rangers winger, 19, earned his first cap against Japan in March and has caught the eye of Clarke after that loan spell during the second half of the campaign.

At the top end of the pitch, Stewart's only two caps came in June 2022, but he is now on the plane to the USA after an impressive end to the season at Southampton.

Image: Ross Stewart has scored nine Championship goals for Southampton despite missing 16 games over the winter due to injury

He'll be joined by Hearts captain Lawrence Shankland, who scored 16 goals in a season where he almost fired the club to the league title, plus Ipswich's George Hirst, who featured in every qualification squad, and the duo Clarke has relied upon most - Che Adams and Lyndon Dykes.

With the squad named, attention now turns to two final warm-up matches against Curacao on May 30 at Hampden Park, before facing Bolivia in the USA.
